title: Deterministic Verification with a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused for both episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent using gpt-5-mini for N = 250 intent pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic validator; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial generations + 1 repair). Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. The preregistered sim‑to‑real/production-like confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition described in the preregistration. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle (manifest) referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as intent-to-configuration translators for network operations (NetOps). They promise rapid, natural-language-driven composition of device CLI sequences, but stochastic generation can produce syntax errors, incorrect ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties that pose operational risk. One pragmatic architecture to reduce mechanically verifiable errors interposes a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance and permits bounded automated repair (a generate–verify–repair, GVR, pattern). Prior work documents that GVR-like pipelines reduce syntactic and simple semantic errors but leaves open how much marginal benefit such guardrails provide when modern LLMs already frequently emit validator-conformant candidates under constrained tasks.

Research question and contribution. We ask: when the same natural-language intent is realized by a single LLM-generated candidate that is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate), what is the paired difference in verifier-confirmed intent-satisfaction between (a) accepting the candidate (baseline) and (b) running a deterministic validator and allowing at most one automated repair (guarded)? Our contributions are (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal validator+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics; (2) a complete reconciliation of provider-call accounting showing model_calls_used = 251 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 250, repair: 1}; and (3) exact paired statistical inference and confidence bounds grounded in archived analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and empirical NetOps studies document that LLMs can produce usable draft configurations in controlled setups but often require verification or oversight [1],[2]. Deterministic network-verification tools and header-space/model-checking techniques (Batfish and related work) are mature for mechanized checks (reachability, local policies) and are commonly proposed as validators in GVR pipelines [3],[4]. Generate-and-verify and program-repair flows have been shown to increase detection and correction rates for mechanically checkable defects in code and configuration domains, though deeper semantic correctness and vendor heterogeneity remain challenging [5],[6]. Security analyses emphasize prompt-injection and retrieval threats to LLM-integrated pipelines and motivate filtering/validation layers, while noting adaptive adversaries remain an open threat [7].

This study differs from prior work by using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that measures the validator/repair marginal effect on identical model outputs and by archiving full validator traces, provider-call accounting, and reconciliation artifacts to permit deterministic audit of the numerical outcomes.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 before execution. The confirmatory design specified N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one initial generation per intent reused by both episodes), a single permitted automated repair per episode, and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration artifact SHA-256 is 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede (archived). The preregistered primary test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired binary outcomes and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729).

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task encoded initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields and workflow constraints (make-before-break, paired MTU change patterns, group-activity constraints). Tasks were intentionally varied in difficulty labels (medium/hard/very_hard) and focused on operationally meaningful composite CLI sequences.

Model invocation and pipeline. All initial shared-generation calls used the declared model gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). For each pair we executed one shared initial-generation call; the same candidate was scored for baseline and guarded episodes (no independent first-pass generations per condition). The guarded pipeline submitted the candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation (syntactic parsing, required_sequence ordering checks, final_state snapshot comparison, and workflow-policy checks). If the validator returned valid = false in a guarded episode, the pipeline allowed up to one template-driven automated repair (syntactic/order fixes only) and re-ran the validator. Repair templates were deterministic and limited to reordering, command splitting, and trivial token-level fixes; multi-iteration repair or human escalation were disallowed by design.

Inclusion, contamination, and exclusions. Preregistered exclusion rules removed items whose vendor-parsers failed deterministically to permit verification or outputs containing denylist/credential artifacts. Contamination detectors flagged instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged items would be excluded from the primary analysis. The preregistration specified treating incomplete pairs as exclusions in primary analysis with sensitivity analyses available.

Analysis plan. Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1: report complete_pair_count, contingency counts (n11,n10,n01,n00), absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline), exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Secondary and sensitivity analyses were prespecified but are reported here as exploratory where executed.
sections.results:
Execution and reconciliation. Execution completed the confirmatory synthetic/emulation partition with planned_episode_count = 500 and completed_episode_count = 500. Provider-call reconciliation recorded model_calls_used = 251, which reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call; adapter audit stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}. No confirmatory episodes were excluded or flagged for contamination; complete_pair_count = 250.

Primary binary outcomes. Deterministic validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Observed contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant cell (n10 = 1) corresponds to the single exercised repair that converted the failing baseline candidate into a guarded pass; the repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided p-value (discordant counts n10 = 1, n01 = 0) = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline difference (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.012] (0 – 1.2 percentage points). These numeric outputs and the bootstrap parameters are archived in the analysis log artifacts.

Representative validator diagnostics and repair trace. Representative scoring artifacts show parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count for passed episodes (for example, task-000003: parsed_command_count = required_command_count = 6 and valid = true). Only one automated repair executed; its trace shows a deterministic reordering fix that satisfied the validator on re-submission. No other repairs were required for the confirmatory partition.

Missingness and exclusions. No episodes were excluded from the primary analysis: analysis/missingness_summary reports complete_pairs = 250 and all other missingness counts = 0. Contamination detectors flagged no confirmatory episodes.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation task bank, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 tasks and the guarded pipeline converted the only failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 pp) bounds the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement under these conditions.

Why the observed gain is small. Artifact-grounded factors that explain the near-null marginal effect include: (1) constrained tasks and deterministic task-generator payloads that reduce ambiguity and encourage well-formed CLI sequences; (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained prompts; and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties and does not measure broader behavioral correctness in live execution or emergent cross-device interactions.

Power, assumptions, and realized baseline rate. The preregistration power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to detect a 15 pp absolute effect with ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) exceeded that assumption substantially and thereby reduced power to detect small absolute improvements; this departure from the power assumption limits inferential sensitivity for small effects and motivates interpreting the bootstrap CI as the primary practical bound.

Scope, threats, and external validity. Internal validity: results depend on prompt templates, single-repair policy, shared_initial_candidate semantics, and the validator encoding. Construct validity: the deterministic validator measured syntax, required_sequence ordering, and final_state snapshots but not live protocol behavior or emergent interactions. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed in this run. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised. Multi-model, multi-iteration repairs, human escalation, and production heterogeneity remain open avenues for further evaluation.

Practical implication. For tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single repair may be small; this finding should not be generalized to broader or adversarial operational contexts without additional evidence. Validators that check richer or production-relevant properties, multi-iteration repairs, or human-in-the-loop escalation may still provide substantial operational benefit in other settings.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the marginal verifier-detected benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). The preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast was not executed; the reported confirmatory estimand is therefore limited to the synthetic/emulation partition. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. All execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this paper are archived in the study evidence bundle and are available for deterministic audit as described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: after an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and conducted pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models, tools, and high-level artifacts: declared model = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses); deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode. Provider-call accounting reconciles to model_calls_used = 251 with stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 250, repair: 1}.

Preregistration and immutable master prompt: preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba).

Evidence-bundle pointer: the full execution and analysis manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, deterministic reconciliation, and the per-artifact hash manifest are archived together; a single manifest file (execution/execution_manifest.json) inside the evidence bundle provides the complete per-file hash listing and machine-verifiable reconciliation. Readers wishing deterministic audit can retrieve the evidence bundle and consult that manifest for full artifact-level hashes and paths. Key numeric reconciliation facts quoted in the paper (for example, model_calls_used = 251; stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 250, repair: 1}; contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; bootstrap parameters seed = 1729, resamples = 10,000) are reproducible from the archived manifests and the manifest-entry indexing.

Executed estimand and deviation disclosure: the preregistration included multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a preregistered sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure: the preregistered sim-to-real/production-like confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250; shared_initial_candidate semantics). The preregistration, master-prompt reference, and the evidence manifest are archived as specified above.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, required_sequence, final_state snapshot) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adaptive adversaries and retrieval-based prompt-injection attacks were not exercised and remain an open operational threat.

Realized baseline pass rate (0.996) departed substantially from the preregistered power assumption (~0.90), reducing power to detect small absolute improvements and making the bootstrap CI the most informative practical bound.
